title: How can I prevent my solar panels from shutting down?
excerpt: Do your solar panels often fail to work on sunny days? It may be that solar panels shut down and that this is the cause. Read more here.
contentHtml:
Do your solar panels often fail to work on sunny days? If so, there is a chance that your solar panels are shutting down. In this blog, we explain what is likely to be the cause and how our product can help. Read on to find out more.

Why are my solar panels stopping working?

If you have solar panels, the following situation will probably sound familiar: it’s a beautiful day and the sun is shining from morning until late afternoon, when suddenly your solar panels stop producing electricity. And your neighbors with solar panels probably have the same problem; their solar panels suddenly stop working too. On very sunny days, solar panels should work extra well, so why do they all stop working? The fact that several people are experiencing this problem at the same time is no coincidence, because it has the same cause: grid congestion. Specifically, this means that the electricity grid is overloaded, making it unsafe to continue operating solar panels, which then shut down.

What is network congestion?

Simply put, grid congestion means that the amount of electricity supplied to the low-voltage grid is too high in relation to consumption. The low-voltage grid refers to the part of the electricity grid to which homes are connected. When solar panels generate electricity, this electricity is first used by appliances connected in the home. If there is any solar power left over, it is fed back into the low-voltage grid. However, if many homes in a neighborhood have solar panels, the amount of electricity fed back into the grid becomes too high. [1] The average voltage of the low-voltage grid is around 230 volts, but too much electricity fed back can cause this to rise to over 250 volts. [2] For safety reasons, solar panel inverters are automatically switched off when the grid voltage exceeds 253 volts. Since an inverter is needed to make solar power usable for appliances, this effectively also switches off the solar panels.

Bron [1]: Solar Magazine | Bron [2]: Ecoburen

What can I do to prevent network congestion?

The simplest solution to grid congestion is to increase your own consumption, so that less power is sent to the grid. However, this is not a particularly elegant solution, as some devices are not useful in this way and someone must be present to turn them on. On weekends, this is usually not a problem, but on weekdays it is much more difficult. Another option is energy storage, so that the energy is available at a later time without any additional action being required. Home batteries are the best-known option for this, but unfortunately they are usually very expensive. A simpler alternative to a home battery is the WaterAccu from Solyx Energy. This system also stores electricity, but in a different way.

How WaterAccu helps prevent grid congestion

The WaterAccu is a combination of an electric boiler and the Solar iBoost. This system is designed to heat tap water for showering and kitchen use. In most households, this heating is still controlled by gas. With the WaterAccu, however, tap water is heated using unused solar power. Thanks to the Solar iBoost, it constantly measures whether the solar panels are supplying power to the grid, and this power is then diverted to the electric boiler. This not only reduces gas consumption, but also increases the use of solar power.

This means that less power is supplied to the grid, reducing the risk of your solar panels shutting down. If the WaterAccu can use all the electricity generated on a specific day, there is no risk at all that the solar panels will stop working. In the future, the electricity infrastructure may be improved to increase capacity. But until then, Solyx Energy’s WaterAccu offers a simple way to avoid grid congestion and get the most out of your solar panels.
